Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude A (lane the primary UI — the main screens the user sees and taps through, plus navigation and layout) ---
Landed real Regenerate wiring. While I was mid-edit, someone else (looks like Claude B, based on the comment referencing my `renderTodayCardIfNeeded` work) concurrently patched `shareButton` to fix a real bug I hadn't caught: free-tier shares were writing the *watermarked* image to `fullResImagePath`, which their ArchiveScreen fix reads back — meaning the user's own archive would've shown their card with the export watermark baked in permanently. Their fix renders a second unwatermarked copy for the archive path when the share itself was watermarked. My edit landed cleanly alongside it with no overlap — verified there's exactly one `regenerateButton`/`performRegeneration` pair (mine) and their `archiveImage` fix is isolated to `shareButton`.

**What I built:** `today.regenerateButton` now does its real job via `RegenerationDivergenceEngine.regenerate(...)` — free tier gets `.notEntitled`, one-per-day limit enforced via `entry.regenerationNonce` as `regenerationsUsedToday`, both surfaced as honest `actionNote` messages rather than a canned stub. Correctly reuses `entry.recipe.timeOfDay` (frozen at original generation, never recomputed) instead of a fresh `currentTimeOfDay()` read — that's a real domain invariant from the interfaces contract, not something I'd have caught without checking the engine's actual signature again. On success it clears `fullResImagePath`/`thumbnailImagePath` back to empty (the old export no longer matches the new recipe — leaving it set would've made Archive lie about which card belongs to today), calls `CheckInCompletionCoordinator.cardBecameAvailable()` per the decision log's two-call-site rule, and explicitly calls `renderTodayCardIfNeeded()` again.

That last part matters: last round I claimed the `.task(id:)` keyed on the recipe would "automatically re-trigger" a fresh render when regeneration lands "for free." Building it for real this round, I caught that claim was wrong — `.task(id:)` only re-fires when SwiftUI re-evaluates the view body, and regeneration doesn't touch `flowState` (same mood/chips, same `.revealed` case), so nothing would force that re-evaluation. Correcting it now with an explicit call rather than let a stale assumption ship silently.

**Left alone:** the button stays always-tappable (never `.disabled` based on entitlement/limit) — I weighed "visibly disabled with a reason" against the risk of changing a UI-crawl-targeted control's hit-testability for the common default (free-tier) case, and picked the lower-risk option: honest post-tap messaging instead of proactive graying-out. Also didn't touch the reveal/share double-render inefficiency — still real, still bounded, still not worth reopening `Rendering/AuraRenderer.swift` right after two lanes stabilized it.

**Can't verify:** same as every round — no compiler access, manual review only.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:

(I'd initially flagged a mismatch against interfaces.json's older `.perturb` name, but that's the same kind of stale-contract drift already noted for `ModelContainerFactory` — the real code is internally consistent, no bug.)
- Confirmed `regenerationsUsedToday: entry.regenerationNonce` is correct despite looking like a nonce/count conflation: since the engine's limit is hardcoded to 1 (`regenerationsUsedToday < 1`), any nonce >0 after a successful regeneration correctly blocks a second one that day regardless of how many retry-forward attempts the divergence guarantee needed. Not a bug.
- Confirmed regeneration correctly clears `fullResImagePath`/`thumbnailImagePath` to `""` on success — this protects my Archive thumbnail fix from last turn (grid correctly falls back to the honest placeholder post-regeneration instead of showing stale pre-regeneration art) and composes correctly with my `shareButton` watermark fix (a post-regeneration share persists a fresh unwatermarked render tied to the new recipe, not leftover data).
- No file overlap: my `archiveImage` fix in `shareButton` (lines ~415-473) is untouched and isolated from Claude A's new `regenerateButton`/`performRegeneration` (475+). Confirmed by direct read, not just trusting the report.
- No conflicts seen.
